guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Intercom, so prototypes work without your own app. Production with your own branding needs your own Intercom public app and approval.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, because Composio provides a managed Intercom OAuth app. For production with your brand on the consent screen and dedicated quota, bring your own public app, which Intercom must approve.
reasons: Consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers
Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need

scenarios.label: Private app on your own workspace
scenarios.when_this_applies: The app only accesses data from your own paid Intercom workspace and no other customers connect.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: Docs say private apps on your own paid workspace need no review (c2).

scenarios.approval: No review for private apps that only access your own paid workspace data.
extras: Only your own workspace's data is accessible

modifiers.note: Only your own workspace's data is accessible

scenarios.label: Public app for other Intercom customers
scenarios.when_this_applies: Customers outside your company install the app through OAuth, either listed in the App Store or unlisted and installed from your own site.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count (OAuth setup, listing, review video), not measured

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "Up to 7 business days per review round").

scenarios.approval: Intercom team reviews the app, its OAuth scopes and its working OAuth flow. Both listed and unlisted public apps must be submitted for review.
extras: Private to you and your team during review
Changes to approved apps need re-approval
Naming and logo rules; developer terms apply

modifiers.note: Private to you and your team during review
Changes to approved apps need re-approval
Naming and logo rules; developer terms apply

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace and Developer Hub app
prerequisites.detail: Private apps rely on your own paid workspace. Public apps are configured in the Developer Hub, where OAuth must be set up before you can submit for review.

prerequisites.title: Terms of service and privacy policy URLs
prerequisites.detail: The listing requires public URLs for your company's terms of service and privacy policy. Paid apps also need a pricing page URL or a sales contact path.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets and test access
prerequisites.detail: You need a 512x512 PNG icon and marketing-format images of at least 1600x1000 PNG under 21MB. If your service needs an account, supply test credentials or setup instructions.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can add several, and the first is the default.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: In the Developer Hub, create the app and tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page. Add redirect URLs and choose scopes.
steps.done_when: Redirect URLs and permissions are saved.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Draft the smallest scope list matching your actual functionality, with a justification for each. Over-privileged scopes are the most common rejection reason.
inputs: List of API calls your agent makes
steps.done_when: Each scope maps to a feature that is demonstrated.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret from the Basic Information page. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Developer Hub.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and the redirect URI matches.

steps.title: Complete listing and Partner Program pages
steps.detail: Fill in the App Listing and App Partner Program pages with company details, use cases and contacts. Fill in the Installation status section if listing in the App Store.

steps.title: Record the OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Record installation with OAuth, the full app functionality and uninstallation, showing the full client_id and state in the OAuth URL.
steps.done_when: Video covers install, features and uninstall.

steps.title: Submit app for review
steps.detail: Submit the app to the Intercom team. Rejected apps must be fixed and resubmitted.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: A review can take up to seven business days. If changes are requested, fix and resubmit.

steps.title: Go live
steps.detail: After approval, the app is unlisted and installed via your own site. To appear in the App Store, select List in App store.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes get apps rejected
traps.detail: This is the most common initial rejection reason. You may be asked to adjust scopes and resubmit.

traps.title: Incomplete video means resubmission
traps.detail: If the video omits any functionality or OAuth steps, you must resubmit it. Each resubmission can take up to seven business days.

traps.title: Region matters for the authorization host
traps.detail: Intercom hosts workspaces in three regions with separate authorization hosts. For customers who sign in with Google, the wrong regional host fails.

traps.title: Changes after approval need re-approval
traps.detail: The app stays public with its current functionality until updates are approved.

traps.title: Naming and logo rules
traps.detail: Names cannot contain 'Intercom' and icons cannot include the Intercom logo, or the app will not be approved.

blockers.what_it_means: Intercom found scope, video or listing problems.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit. Allow up to seven more business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review your scope list against your demonstrated features and check listing fields.

open_questions: Is there any approval time beyond 'up to seven business days'? Ask Intercom developer support or check the yellow banner in the Developer Hub.
Does a specific scope set trigger extra scrutiny (the scopes page was not found)? Check the Developer Hub scope list or ask Intercom developer support.
Can customers' admins block installation? The docs do not mention any admin approval step; test with a customer workspace.
